source: AB Pic b spins in about 2.1 hours (Palma-Bifani et al. 2023, Abstract), and its true obliquity is about 45 or 135 degrees, but the direction of its axis on the sky is not measured; no spin is propagated. The display axis is the normal of its hosted orbit in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/ab-pic-b.json, computed by hostedKeplerElements in @cssearth/astronomy; the meridian is set so that grid longitude 0 faces the Sun and Earth at the scene epoch.
coordinateSystem: ICRF/J2000. +Z is the display axis, the orbit normal; +X is the display meridian; east longitude. No spin is propagated.
qualification: Display convention, not a measurement: the spin axis, spin sense, period and prime meridian of AB Pic b are unmeasured; the axis shown is its orbit normal.
